--- header_pre ---
#define j0 _j0

#define y0 _y0
#define y1 _y1
#define yn _yn
#define gamma _gamma
#define lgamma _lgamma
#define tgamma _tgamma
#include <stddef.h>

#ifndef M_PI
#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846
#endif

static float g_angle = 0.0f;
static int   g_rotating = 0;

--- display_header ---
void display(void) {
  glLoadIdentity();
  glPushAttrib(GL_ALL_ATTRIB_BITS);
--- lights_pre_camera ---
--- camera ---
  // camera
  glTranslatef(0.0000f, 0.0000f, -19.0000f);
  glRotatef(30.0000f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
  glRotatef(0.0000f, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
  glTranslatef(-0.0000f, -0.0000f, -0.0000f);
--- header_post ---
--- render_state ---
  glEnable(GL_MULTISAMPLE);
  glDisable(GL_LINE_SMOOTH);
  float A[16], B[16], C[16];
--- source ---
  static float px, py, pz; // planet position - the caller hangs a label off it
  static float orbitR; // log-compressed orbit radius, shared by the draw funcs
  static float ASTEROIDS = 280; // @tune
  static float EARTH_R = 0.17; // @tune
  static float EARTH_RATE = 0.85; // @tune
  static float ORB_BASE = 0; // @tune
  static float ORB_SCALE = 10; // @tune
  static float decYr, yr, leap, doy, mon, day; // calendar readout scratch
  static float astAng; // asteroid belt orbit angle


  orbitRings(Drel, node, incl) {
    float th, u;
    orbitR = ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + Drel);
    glBegin(GL_LINE_LOOP);
      for(i, 0, 96) {
        th = i*TAU/96;
        u = th - node;
        glVertex3f(orbitR*(cos(node)*cos(u) - sin(node)*sin(u)*cos(incl)), orbitR*sin(u)*sin(incl), orbitR*(sin(node)*cos(u) + cos(node)*sin(u)*cos(incl)));
      }
    glEnd();
  }
  // planet(): one lit sphere on an inclined circular orbit. The caller passes
  // TRUE ratios relative to Earth: distance from Sun (Drel), year length (Yrel),
  // J2000 heliocentric longitude phase, J2000 node/inclination, and body radius
  // (Rrel). The display applies documented compression for orbit distance and
  // sphere size only.
  // px/py/pz stay set after the call so the caller can hang a label off the
  // body. th/u are function-scoped locals (plain `float` inside the body, no
  // `static`), so they are private to one call and cost no variable-panel
  // slot. t=0 is year 2000.0 (J2000 alignment).
  planet(Drel, Yrel, phase, node, incl, Rrel, cr, cg, cb) {
    float th, u;
    orbitR = ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + Drel);
    th = phase + t*EARTH_RATE/Yrel;
    u = th - node;
    th = orbitR*cos(u);
    u = orbitR*sin(u);
    px = th*cos(node) - u*sin(node)*cos(incl);
    py = u*sin(incl);
    pz = th*sin(node) + u*cos(node)*cos(incl);
    glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
    glColor3f(cr, cg, cb);
    glPushMatrix();
      glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
      glutSolidSphere(EARTH_R * pow(Rrel, 1.0/3.0), 24, 18);
    glPopMatrix();
    glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  }
  planetKepler(a0, adot, e0, edot, I0, Idot, L0, Ldot, peri0, peridot, node0, nodedot, Rrel, cr, cg, cb) {
    float th, u;
    float aK, eK, iK, lK, pK, nK, mK, eAn;
    float xh, yh, x1, y1, z1;
    th = t*EARTH_RATE/TAU/100.0; // Julian centuries since J2000.0
    aK = a0 + adot*th;
    eK = e0 + edot*th;
    iK = (I0 + Idot*th)*PI/180;
    lK = (L0 + Ldot*th)*PI/180;
    pK = (peri0 + peridot*th)*PI/180;
    nK = (node0 + nodedot*th)*PI/180;
    mK = rem(lK - pK, TAU);
    // Solve Kepler's equation M = E - e*sin(E) for the eccentric anomaly eAn
    // via Newton's method: seed with mK, then 4 fixed refinement iterations.
    eAn = mK + eK*sin(mK);
    eAn = eAn + (mK - (eAn - eK*sin(eAn)))/(1 - eK*cos(eAn));
    eAn = eAn + (mK - (eAn - eK*sin(eAn)))/(1 - eK*cos(eAn));
    eAn = eAn + (mK - (eAn - eK*sin(eAn)))/(1 - eK*cos(eAn));
    eAn = eAn + (mK - (eAn - eK*sin(eAn)))/(1 - eK*cos(eAn));
    // 1. Calculate 2D position in orbital plane relative to perihelion
    xh = aK*(cos(eAn) - eK);
    yh = aK*sqrt(1 - eK*eK)*sin(eAn);

    // 2. Compute heliocentric distance (vector length is invariant under 3D
    // rotations). Reuse eAn (done with the eccentric anomaly now) to hold the
    // radius r, staying inside this function's MAX_EXPR_VARS scope (16
    // parameters + 15 locals = 31 of 32).
    eAn = sqrt(xh*xh + yh*yh);
    orbitR = ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + eAn);

    // 3. Decompose 3D rotation: Step A: Rotate in orbital plane by argument of perihelion (u = pK - nK)
    // to align position relative to the ascending node line. Reuse aK, eK as xo, yo to stay inside the scope cap.
    u = pK - nK;
    aK = xh*cos(u) - yh*sin(u);
    eK = xh*sin(u) + yh*cos(u);

    // 4. Decompose 3D rotation: Step B: Project from node line to ecliptic plane
    // using ascending node longitude (nK) and inclination (iK)
    x1 = aK*cos(nK) - eK*sin(nK)*cos(iK);
    y1 = aK*sin(nK) + eK*cos(nK)*cos(iK);
    z1 = eK*sin(iK);

    // 5. Scale 3D unit direction vector by logarithmic orbit radius
    px = orbitR*x1/eAn;
    py = orbitR*z1/eAn;
    pz = orbitR*y1/eAn;
    glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
    glColor3f(cr, cg, cb);
    glPushMatrix();
      glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
      glutSolidSphere(EARTH_R * pow(Rrel, 1.0/3.0), 24, 18);
    glPopMatrix();
    glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  }
  glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
  glEnable(GL_COLOR_MATERIAL);
  glColorMaterial(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_AMBIENT_AND_DIFFUSE);
  glLightModeli(GL_LIGHT_MODEL_TWO_SIDE, GL_TRUE);
  glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SPECULAR, (GLfloat[]){0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 1});
  glMaterialf(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SHININESS, 30);
  glClearColor(0.02, 0.02, 0.05, 1);
  glEnable(GL_NORMALIZE);
  glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE);
  glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);

  // planets: opaque, lit by the central SOLAR light. Blending stays OFF here
  // so each body is a solid sphere - planets never blend with one another.
  // Only the sun's corona (drawn last, additive) glows over them. glColor
  // rides GL_COLOR_MATERIAL and one shared specular material gives every body
  // a sun-glint.
  glEnable(GL_LIGHT0);
  glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SPECULAR, (GLfloat[]){0.35, 0.33, 0.3, 1});
  glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SHININESS, (GLfloat[]){18});
  // Body sizes: R/E is the true radius relative to Earth; "display" is what
  // this scene draws after the cube-root squash (display = EARTH_R*R/E^(1/3)),
  // which keeps the 0.38..11x planet span legible. The Sun (109x!) is off the
  // chart, so it stays a hand-tuned "hero" size rather than on the planet rule.
  //   +---------+--------+---------+
  //   | Body    |   R/E  | display |
  //   +---------+--------+---------+
  //   | Mercury |  0.383 |  0.124  |
  //   | Venus   |  0.950 |  0.167  |
  //   | Earth   |  1.000 |  0.170  |
  //   | Mars    |  0.532 |  0.138  |
  //   | Jupiter | 10.97  |  0.378  |
  //   | Saturn  |  9.14  |  0.356  |
  //   | Uranus  |  3.98  |  0.269  |
  //   | Neptune |  3.86  |  0.267  |
  //   | Sun     | 109.2  |  hero   |
  //   +---------+--------+---------+
  //
  // Orbit speeds: Y/E is the true year length relative to Earth. The circular
  // planets use rate = EARTH_RATE/Y/E. Earth and Mars use JPL Keplerian element
  // rates in planetKepler() below. t=0 is year 2000.0:
  // Year = 2000 + t*EARTH_RATE/TAU.
  // | Body    | Year length relative to Earth |
  // | ------- | ----------------------------: |
  // | Mercury |                     **0.241** |
  // | Venus   |                     **0.615** |
  // | Earth   |                     **1.000** |
  // | Mars    |                     **1.881** |
  // | Jupiter |                     **11.86** |
  // | Saturn  |                     **29.46** |
  // | Uranus  |                      **84.0** |
  // | Neptune |                     **164.8** |
  // | Sun     |                       **N/A** |
  //
  // J2000 alignment: for circular planets, the phase argument is approximate
  // heliocentric ecliptic longitude at 2000-01-01 12:00 TT, computed from JPL
  // low-precision elements. Earth and Mars use mean longitude/perihelion rates
  // instead so their relative phase should align with real opposition dates.
  // | Body    | J2000 heliocentric longitude |
  // | ------- | ---------------------------: |
  // | Mercury |                   253.78 deg |
  // | Venus   |                   182.61 deg |
  // | Earth   |                   100.38 deg |
  // | Mars    |                   359.45 deg |
  // | Jupiter |                    36.38 deg |
  // | Saturn  |                    45.58 deg |
  // | Uranus  |                   316.40 deg |
  // | Neptune |                   303.92 deg |
  // | Sun     |                         N/A  |
  //
  // Orbit planes: node/incl arguments use JPL J2000 longitude of ascending node
  // and inclination relative to the J2000 ecliptic. Scene axes map ecliptic
  // x/y/z to displayed x/z/y, so the ecliptic plane remains the main xz plane.
  // | Body    | Inclination | Ascending node |
  // | ------- | ----------: | -------------: |
  // | Mercury |   7.005 deg |      48.33 deg |
  // | Venus   |   3.395 deg |      76.68 deg |
  // | Earth   |   0.000 deg |       0.00 deg |
  // | Mars    |   1.850 deg |      49.56 deg |
  // | Jupiter |   1.304 deg |     100.47 deg |
  // | Saturn  |   2.486 deg |     113.66 deg |
  // | Uranus  |   0.773 deg |      74.02 deg |
  // | Neptune |   1.770 deg |     131.78 deg |
  // | Sun     |         N/A |            N/A |
  //
  // Orbit distances: D/E is the true mean distance from the Sun relative to
  // Earth. planet() and orbitRings() display it with a log scale:
  // orbitR = ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + D/E). log() is base-10 in the REPL.
  // The large scale pushes the inner system outward, while the log term spreads
  // Mercury/Venus/Earth more than a cube-root fit. The Sun stays at the origin
  // and does not use the formula.
  // | Body    | Distance from Sun relative to Earth |
  // | ------- | ----------------------------------: |
  // | Mercury |                           **0.387** |
  // | Venus   |                           **0.723** |
  // | Earth   |                           **1.000** |
  // | Mars    |                           **1.524** |
  // | Jupiter |                           **5.203** |
  // | Saturn  |                           **9.537** |
  // | Uranus  |                           **19.19** |
  // | Neptune |                           **30.07** |
  // | Sun     |                     **0.000 / N/A** |
  // Mercury (0.383 Earth radii, 0.241 Earth years)
  planet(0.387, 0.241, 253.78*PI/180, 48.33*PI/180, 7.005*PI/180, 0.383, 0.63, 0.58, 0.54);
  glColor3f(0.9, 0.85, 0.8);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.14, py + 0.16, pz);
  label("Mercury");
  // Venus (0.950 Earth radii, 0.615 Earth years)
  planet(0.723, 0.615, 182.61*PI/180, 76.68*PI/180, 3.395*PI/180, 0.950, 0.93, 0.81, 0.55);
  glColor3f(1, 0.9, 0.65);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.2, py + 0.22, pz);
  label("Venus");
  // Earth and Mars use JPL low-precision Keplerian elements/rates instead of
  // circular phase advance. These two phases should be accurate enough to align
  // with real Mars-Earth opposition dates; the other planets remain visual.
  // Earth (the reference radius) + Moon circling it
  planetKepler(1.00000261, 0.00000562, 0.01671123, -0.00004392, -0.00001531, -0.01294668, 100.46457166, 35999.37244981, 102.93768193, 0.32327364, 0, 0, 1.000, 0.3, 0.52, 0.95);
  glPushMatrix();
    glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
    glRotatef(t*160, 0, 1, 0);
    glTranslatef(0.25, 0.06, 0);
    glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
    glColor3f(0.72, 0.72, 0.7);
    glutSolidSphere(0.046, 12, 10);
    glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glPopMatrix();
  glColor3f(0.6, 0.8, 1);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.2, py + 0.22, pz);
  label("Earth");
  // Mars (0.532 Earth radii, 1.881 Earth years)
  planetKepler(1.52371034, 0.00001847, 0.09339410, 0.00007882, 1.84969142, -0.00813131, -4.55343205, 19140.30268499, -23.94362959, 0.44441088, 49.55953891, -0.29257343, 0.532, 0.88, 0.45, 0.26);
  glColor3f(1, 0.6, 0.45);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.16, py + 0.18, pz);
  label("Mars");
  // Jupiter (10.97 Earth radii, 11.86 Earth years)
  planet(5.203, 11.86, 36.38*PI/180, 100.47*PI/180, 1.304*PI/180, 10.97, 0.83, 0.69, 0.52);
  glColor3f(1, 0.85, 0.65);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.62, py + 0.5, pz);
  label("Jupiter");
  // Saturn (9.14 Earth radii, 29.46 Earth years) + two ring bands with a
  // Cassini gap.
  // Rings are translucent flat strips, so blending is on (additive, like the
  // corona) and culling is off while they draw - either face may point at the
  // camera. Depth writes are masked so the bands don't clip each other.
  planet(9.537, 29.46, 45.58*PI/180, 113.66*PI/180, 2.486*PI/180, 9.14, 0.9, 0.8, 0.58);
  glPushMatrix();
    glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
    glRotatef(27, 1, 0, 0.35);
    glDisable(GL_CULL_FACE);
    glEnable(GL_BLEND);
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
    glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
    glBegin(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP);
      for(s, 0, 33) {
        glColor4f(0.85, 0.75, 0.55, 0.5);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.66, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.66);
        glColor4f(0.9, 0.82, 0.6, 0.3);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.88, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.88);
      }
    glEnd();
    glBegin(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP);
      for(s, 0, 33) {
        glColor4f(0.8, 0.72, 0.5, 0.35);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.93, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.93);
        glColor4f(0.75, 0.68, 0.48, 0.12);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*1.05, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*1.05);
      }
    glEnd();
    glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
    glDisable(GL_BLEND);
    glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE);
  glPopMatrix();
  glColor3f(1, 0.9, 0.7);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 1.1, py + 0.4, pz);
  label("Saturn");
  // Uranus (3.98 Earth radii, 84.0 Earth years) + a thin ring standing nearly on
  // end:
  // the planet is tipped ~98 degrees, so its rings face the sun pole-on
  planet(19.19, 84.0, 316.40*PI/180, 74.02*PI/180, 0.773*PI/180, 3.98, 0.58, 0.82, 0.88);
  glPushMatrix();
    glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
    glRotatef(98, 0, 0, 1);
    glDisable(GL_CULL_FACE);
    glEnable(GL_BLEND);
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
    glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
    glBegin(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP);
      for(s, 0, 33) {
        glColor4f(0.72, 0.88, 0.92, 0.4);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.44, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.44);
        glColor4f(0.72, 0.88, 0.92, 0.1);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.58, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.58);
      }
    glEnd();
    glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
    glDisable(GL_BLEND);
    glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE);
  glPopMatrix();
  glColor3f(0.75, 0.92, 0.95);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.6, py + 0.35, pz);
  label("Uranus");
  // Neptune (3.86 Earth radii, 164.8 Earth years)
  planet(30.07, 164.8, 303.92*PI/180, 131.78*PI/180, 1.770*PI/180, 3.86, 0.28, 0.42, 0.9);
  glColor3f(0.55, 0.65, 1);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.42, py + 0.34, pz);
  label("Neptune");
  // live readout: exact Gregorian calendar date, anchored in 3D below the system.
  // The decimal sim year is split into year / month / day with real month lengths
  // (leap years included via the 4/100/400 rule), so the readout tracks a true
  // calendar to the day. The if/else-if chain peels off whole months; flatten
  // evaluates it each frame, emitting only the live branch. t=0 is 2000-1-1.
  decYr = 2000 + t*EARTH_RATE/TAU; // decimal year
  yr = floor(decYr); // integer year
  leap = (fmod(yr, 4) == 0 && fmod(yr, 100) != 0) || fmod(yr, 400) == 0; // 1 in leap years
  doy = floor((decYr - yr)*(365 + leap)); // day of year, 0-based
  if(doy < 31) {
    mon = 1;
    day = doy + 1;
  } else if(doy < 59 + leap) {
    mon = 2;
    day = doy - 31 + 1;
  } else if(doy < 90 + leap) {
    mon = 3;
    day = doy - 59 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 120 + leap) {
    mon = 4;
    day = doy - 90 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 151 + leap) {
    mon = 5;
    day = doy - 120 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 181 + leap) {
    mon = 6;
    day = doy - 151 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 212 + leap) {
    mon = 7;
    day = doy - 181 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 243 + leap) {
    mon = 8;
    day = doy - 212 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 273 + leap) {
    mon = 9;
    day = doy - 243 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 304 + leap) {
    mon = 10;
    day = doy - 273 - leap + 1;
  } else if(doy < 334 + leap) {
    mon = 11;
    day = doy - 304 - leap + 1;
  } else {
    mon = 12;
    day = doy - 334 - leap + 1;
  }
  glColor3f(0.75, 0.8, 0.9);
  glRasterPos3f(-2.6, -5.6, 0);
  label("Date %f-%f-%f", yr, mon, day);

  // Asteroid belt: a decorative dusty band between Mars and Jupiter (the main
  // belt, ~2.2-3.3 AU). Not physical - each speck is scattered with rand() onto
  // its own near-circular orbit, drifting at the Kepler rate for its radius
  // (EARTH_RATE/a^1.5, so inner specks lap the outer ones) and riding the same
  // log-distance scale as the planets. Drawn as small unlit points, depth-tested
  // so the planets pass in front of and behind the band.
  glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glEnable(GL_POINT_SMOOTH);
  glPointSize(2);
  glBegin(GL_POINTS);
    for(i, 0, ASTEROIDS) {
      astAng = rand(i, 2)*TAU + t*EARTH_RATE/pow(2.2 + 1.1*rand(i, 1), 1.5);
      glColor3f((0.45 + 0.5*rand(i, 3))*0.55, (0.45 + 0.5*rand(i, 3))*0.48, (0.45 + 0.5*rand(i, 3))*0.4);
      glVertex3f((ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + 2.2 + 1.1*rand(i, 1)))*cos(astAng), rand2(i, 4)*0.35, (ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + 2.2 + 1.1*rand(i, 1)))*sin(astAng));
    }
  glEnd();

  // faint orbit rings (unlit lines), one per planet at its inclination
  glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glColor3f(0.22, 0.24, 0.34);
  glLineWidth(1.2);
  orbitRings(0.387, 48.33*PI/180, 7.005*PI/180);
  orbitRings(0.723, 76.68*PI/180, 3.395*PI/180);
  orbitRings(1.000, 0.0, 0.0);
  orbitRings(1.524, 49.56*PI/180, 1.850*PI/180);
  orbitRings(5.203, 100.47*PI/180, 1.304*PI/180);
  orbitRings(9.537, 113.66*PI/180, 2.486*PI/180);
  orbitRings(19.19, 74.02*PI/180, 0.773*PI/180);
  orbitRings(30.07, 131.78*PI/180, 1.770*PI/180);

  // the sun, drawn LAST so its soft corona composites over the rest of the
  // scene: an additive glow (GL_ONE) that is still depth-tested - planets in
  // front of the sun occlude it, planets behind it receive the glow (so only
  // the corona blends with the planets). Depth writes are masked so the
  // stacked shells don't clip each other; the opaque core then writes depth.
  // Drawn unlit so it glows (it sits on the SOLAR light at the origin).
  glEnable(GL_BLEND);
  glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
  glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
  // soft corona: thin additive shells at constant low alpha - the nested
  // layers accumulate, so brightness ramps smoothly toward the core (a
  // radial falloff). Each shell pulses at a phase offset to keep the
  // shimmer alive.
  glPushMatrix();
    glScalef(1, 0.5, 1);
    for(i, 0, 20) {
      glColor4f(1, 0.75, 0.25, 0.02);
      glutSolidSphere(0.5 + i*0.1 + sin(t*1.3 + i*0.7)*0.052, 24, 24);
    }
  glPopMatrix();
  glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
  glDisable(GL_BLEND);
  glColor4f(1, 0.85, 0.3, 0.5);
  glutSolidSphere(0.45, 24, 24);
  glDisable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);
  glColor3f(1, 0.72, 0);
  glRasterPos3f(0.62, 0.58, 0);
  label("Sun");
